# Signet Artists

> Whether it's a jazz trio vibe while your guests find the bar, or a party on the dance floor, we've got you covered. Signet artists provides high quality, professional live music for private events across Colorado: from a single DJ to a 13 piece band all on one contract.

Signet Artists is a live music company for private events in Denver, the Front Range, and the mountain corridor. Rates are published rather than quoted on request; the full card is on the pricing page.

## Pages

- [Check a Date](https://signetartists.com/contact/): Tell us the date, the room and the guest count. Availability and an exact number back inside 24 to 48 hours, in business hours.

- [Corporate holiday party bands and DJs in Denver, November and December 2026](https://signetartists.com/corporate/holiday/): Live music and DJs for Denver corporate holiday parties, November and December 2026. Open dates published, rates published, from $1,500. Book August through October for the best dates.

## Acts

- Dirty Flamenco (Flamenco, fronted by Gary Meyers): The only flamenco act on this roster, and close to the only one in Colorado sold as a private event product rather than a concert booking. Real palos, played by a group with a standing book. Book it when the room needs one thing guests photograph. Configurations: Trio to six piece. From $2,800 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/dirty-flamenco/
- Jordan Lovinger & DF (Jazz standards, fronted by Jordan Lovinger): Standards on upright bass and guitar, played at the volume of the room. The booking for arrival, cocktails and dinner, when the music has to hold the room without anybody having to raise their voice over it. Configurations: Duo. From $2,000 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/jordan-lovinger-and-df/
- Tejas Sing (Singer-songwriter covers, fronted by Tejas Sing): The only act here that ladders. A duo at six o'clock and a quartet at ten, same face, same book, one contract. At quartet and up this is the biggest thing on the roster and the one to book when the floor has to fill. Configurations: Duo to six piece. From $2,000 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/tejas-sing/
- Dan Steele (Funk, fronted by Dan Steele): Voice-fronted funk and soul for a small room. The singer is the front of this band, so the set leans on the vocal end of the funk book: Motown, Stax, the songs a room sings back. Book it where the dance floor is close to the tables. Configurations: Trio. From $2,800 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/
- DF Funk (Funk, fronted by Daniel Fox): Guitar-fronted funk, built on the groove rather than the vocal. Instrumental heads, longer pockets, and a set that works as hard at background volume as it does on a floor. The one to book when the room wants funk without a frontman working it. Configurations: Trio. From $2,800 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/
- Thomas Owen Band (Americana, fronted by Thomas Owen): Americana for a patio and the daylight end of an event. Roots, country and folk-rock played by a trio that can sit at conversation volume for three hours without going flat. Outdoor ceremonies, welcome parties and long afternoons. Configurations: Trio. From $2,800 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/
- Josh (DJ, fronted by Josh): Open format DJ, on its own or carrying the late end after a band steps off. Adding a live instrument over the decks, bass or saxophone, is a named option rather than a favor: it is the format roughly one couple in six now asks for, and it is priced on the rate card. Configurations: Solo to duo. From $1,500 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/
- Tony Medina (Blues-based covers, fronted by Tony Medina): Blues-based covers, solo or as a duo, at the smallest spend on this roster. Background music that is actually played rather than streamed. Rehearsal dinners, welcome drinks, office parties and any room where live music is the right idea and a band is the wrong size. Configurations: Solo to duo. From $900 in Denver. https://signetartists.com/music/

## Rate card

Starting prices by configuration. Denver metro, then mountain and resort, which adds travel and lodging.

- Solo: Denver $900–1,200, mountain and resort $1,400–1,900.
- Duo: Denver $2,000–2,800, mountain and resort $2,800–3,800.
- Trio: Denver $2,800–3,800, mountain and resort $3,800–5,200.
- Quartet: Denver $4,000–5,500, mountain and resort $5,500–7,500.
- Five to six piece: Denver $6,000–8,000, mountain and resort $8,000–11,000.
- DJ: Denver $1,500–2,800, mountain and resort $3,000–4,800.
- Corporate band range: Denver $6,000–12,500, mountain and resort $8,000–15,000+.

## Hourly build (Denver metro)

- Duo: $600 call-out + $450/hour. Four hours = $2,400.
- Trio: $1,000 call-out + $600/hour. Four hours = $3,400.
- Quartet: $1,600 call-out + $800/hour. Four hours = $4,800.
- Quintet: $2,200 call-out + $1,000/hour. Four hours = $6,200.
- Seven-piece: $3,500 call-out + $1,250/hour. Four hours = $8,500.
- Ten-piece: $5,300 call-out + $1,800/hour. Four hours = $12,500.
- Thirteen-piece: $8,000 call-out + $2,500/hour. Four hours = $18,000.
- DJ: $800 call-out + $350/hour. Four hours = $2,200.

Price = call-out + (hours x hourly rate). There is no overtime rate. Adding a smaller group to an existing booking bills at the hourly rate only, with no second call-out.
